response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** ESCALATE, with confidence 0.6. Level 2 reviews it. The proposal is on file as case C-A-261009-0007, awaiting a human decision.

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. T-X1009-05 is a PROP trader with no market-making registration and a typical order size of 500. It placed a BUY of 18,930 (7.9× top-5 depth) at 9997, one tick below the bid. It cancelled the whole order after 803 ms.
2. There were no fills of any kind, so there was no opposite-side execution or benefit. There was no repetition in the session and no prior alerts. That rules out a STOR draft.
3. No accepted explanation is supported. There is no market event, risk event, parent order or partial fill. A 1,893 BUY at the same price followed 1.2 seconds later. That is one-tenth the size, so the first order may have been a ×10 entry error, but that is not confirmed.

**What would change my mind:** Confirmation that the 18,930 was a ×10 entry error corrected by the 1,893 order would support closing it as an entry error. An opposite-side execution by this trader just before the cancel, or repeated cycles, would move it toward a STOR draft.
